2 · Paste the post copy

Alaska's order telling every agency to review spending with AI has no end date. A new governor inherits it on December 7th.

Leaving it alone is a decision too.

Mike Dunleavy signed Administrative Order 359 on August 4th, 2025.
Every agency is told to use AI to see how state funds "are actually being spent."
Two of its seven agency duties name AI.
Grants to non-state entities and accounts payable are the first focus areas.
The order puts the Office of Management and Budget in charge.
On November 18th Governor-elect Kreiss-Tomkins named Alexei Painter to lead that office.

Swipe for the AI clause word for word, the order's seven duties and its own 2025 case, then the new budget director and the December 7th handoff.

Should a standing AI order over the budget stay one governor's call, or should the Legislature get a say?

#AlaskaBudget #PublicSectorAI #AlaskaPolitics

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post in the strongest window, Tuesday to Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time (posting cadence is the maintainer's call). If this edition already went out through the automatic Upload-Post delivery, check that the LinkedIn post and its link comment are both live.
  • Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of the post going live.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. No source says whether Kreiss-Tomkins will keep, rewrite or revoke AO 359, or whether OMB published a grants list or review under it, so replies shouldn't claim either way.
  • After 48 hours note saves, comments and reposts for the instincts ledger, and watch for any statement on AO 359 from the incoming administration after December 7th, which would be the follow-up deck.
